etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From disinterest (“to cause to be impartial”, verb) +‎ -ed (suffix forming past tense or past participle forms of verbs), or from dis- (prefix meaning ‘not’) +‎ interested (“having a stake in; showing interest”, adjective).
senses: Having no interest or stake in the outcome, and no conflicts of interest; free of bias, impartial. [from 17th c.]
(often proscribed) Synonym of uninterested (“not interested; not concerned; indifferent”). [from 17th c.]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: simple past and past participle of disinterest
